pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: What's the difference between `scores := make(map[string]int)` and `var scores map[string]int`? What can go wrong with the second?
expected_points: make returns an empty map ready for reads and writes; a literal is the other way to initialize
reading a nil map yields zero values, but writing to it panics at runtime

questions.prompt: Walk me through what `counts[w]++` does the first time a word `w` appears. And how do you remove an entry entirely — what does setting it to 0 do instead?
expected_points: reading a missing key returns the value type's zero value, so ++ stores 1 with no existence check
setting the value to 0 keeps the key present — comma-ok still reports true

questions.prompt: `pantry["eggs"]` gives you 0. What are the two situations that could produce that, and how do you tell them apart?
expected_points: either the key is missing (zero value returned) or the stored value really is 0
v, ok := m[k] — ok reports whether the key exists, independent of the value

questions.prompt: You range over a map and print its entries; two runs print different orders. Is that a bug? What does Go promise, and how do you get stable output?
expected_points: not a bug — iteration order is deliberately randomized so programs can't come to depend on it
collect the keys into a slice, sort it (slices.Sort), then range over the sorted slice

questions.prompt: How do you build a set in Go, and why `map[string]struct{}` rather than `map[string]bool`?
expected_points: keys are the members; membership is a comma-ok lookup
struct{} has no fields and takes zero bytes — the value carries no information
bool invites a misleading false-but-present third state

questions.prompt: `Take` modifies the pantry but never returns it — why does the caller still see the change?
expected_points: a map value is a small handle to shared underlying storage
the function receives a copy of the handle, not of the entries, so mutations are visible to the caller

questions.prompt: Why can't you use a slice as a map key?
expected_points: map keys must be comparable with ==
slices have no == comparison; strings, numbers, and booleans do
